payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Its gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that point. Although an initial press release reported 12,000 cycles, an independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit retracted that figure as improperly normalized and established the corrected cycle life at 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold.
